items.headline: OpenAI acquires Orchestra Bio to expand its Rosalind life-sciences push
items.summary: OpenAI bought the drug-development coordination startup Orchestra Bio and will fold its team and agentic workflow tools into Rosalind, OpenAI's life-sciences model suite. The deal signals frontier AI labs racing to move beyond chat products into automating actual drug-discovery pipelines, following Anthropic's similar biotech push.

items.headline: Google open-sources TorchTPU, bringing native PyTorch support to Cloud TPUs
items.summary: Unveiled at PyTorch Conference, TorchTPU lets existing PyTorch code target Google's TPUs by simply switching the device setting, replacing the older PyTorch/XLA bridge and integrating with vLLM, SGLang, TorchTitan and Hugging Face Transformers. It was co-developed with Meta and tested at a scale of 8,192 Ironwood (TPU7x) chips, lowering the barrier to running PyTorch workloads outside Nvidia's CUDA ecosystem.

items.headline: Anthropic pitches Congress a federal AI safety bill with a high bar for shutting down models
items.summary: Anthropic has privately circulated draft legislation that would let federal authorities halt a frontier AI model only when it poses an imminent risk of over $1 billion in damages or death/injury to more than 50 people, covering bioweapons, loss of control, and cyberattack scenarios. The threshold has drawn criticism from some policy watchers as too permissive, while others see it as a template building on Anthropic's own Advanced AI Framework and California's SB 53.

items.headline: AI chip startup Tenstorrent raises $1.5B Series E at a $6.2B valuation
items.summary: Tenstorrent, the RISC-V/AI accelerator company founded by chip veteran Jim Keller, more than doubled its valuation from its 2024 round with backing from Fidelity, ARK Invest, Morgan Stanley and Tether. The capital will fund volume manufacturing of its Galaxy servers, underscoring continued investor appetite for Nvidia alternatives even as commercial traction remains unproven at scale.

items.headline: Dream Labs raises $90M seed and launches a foundation-model API for robots
items.summary: Dream Labs' new Dream API turns a robot's camera feed and a plain-English instruction into motor commands, with its Dream-1 model already working with more than 20 hardware partners on tasks like picking, placing and folding laundry. The launch adds to a wave of 'robot brain' foundation models aiming to generalize across different manufacturers' hardware.

items.headline: Tesla's AI and robotics capital spending trails Wall Street expectations
items.summary: Tesla's latest quarterly results show spending on AI and robotics initiatives, including Optimus and its AI compute buildout, falling short of analyst forecasts, clouding Elon Musk's plan to pivot the company toward artificial intelligence and robotics. The shortfall raises questions about the pace of Tesla's humanoid robot and self-driving ambitions relative to its public targets.

items.headline: Salesforce to buy marketing platform Braze for $5.66B to bolster Agentforce
items.summary: Salesforce will fold Braze's real-time customer-engagement tools into Marketing Cloud, Data 360 and its Agentforce AI-agent platform, paying a roughly 58% premium over Braze's prior share price. The deal is the latest in Salesforce's string of AI-focused acquisitions as it races to make autonomous agents central to its enterprise software stack.

items.headline: Agility Robotics taps Nyobolt for ultra-fast-charging batteries in its Digit 5 humanoid
items.summary: The partnership gives Digit 5 a roughly 10:1 run-to-charge ratio -- 90 minutes of work per 9-minute charge, versus 2:1 for the prior-generation Digit 4 -- aimed at letting the humanoid work more than 20 hours in a 24-hour day across multiple shifts. Faster charging addresses one of the biggest practical bottlenecks limiting humanoid robot utilization in warehouses and factories.

items.headline: Anthropic's Q3 revenue jumps 45% to $16.8B as it prepares for a possible IPO
items.summary: Anthropic reportedly told potential investors its third-quarter revenue reached $16.8 billion and that the company has achieved adjusted profitability, strengthening its case ahead of a widely anticipated US listing that could rival SpaceX's record IPO size. The disclosure comes as Anthropic also fights a separate legal battle with the Pentagon over a terminated contract.
